Audrey — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts to start: a concise playbook and a retention matrix (see attachments). Summary below; happy to follow up with a short technical call.

High-level export formats
- JSONL (newline-delimited JSON): canonical, ideal for small slices and redaction pipelines. Supports per-event signatures.
- Parquet (columnar): recommended for large-volume bulk exports (storage-efficient, query-friendly).
- Compressed tarballs (gz) containing segmented JSONL + manifest for archive handoffs.
- Streaming export (Kafka-compatible) possible for ongoing replication — typically a separate commercial integration.

Scoping & slicing
- Exports can be scoped by tenant, project, model_id, route, and arbitrary time range.
- We support time-sliced snapshots (hour/day) and incremental delta exports (since-token or since-timestamp) for efficient transfers.
- Policies can be configured per-account: e.g., 90 days hot, 2 years warm, archive at customer-managed S3 after X days.

Retention tiers
- Hot: default 90 days (low-latency access in serving runtime)
- Warm: 1–3 years (compressed, cold storage in Redwoods-managed buckets)
- Archive: customer-managed S3/Glacier options for multi-year retention; we can push bundles on schedule
- Note: custom retention windows per account are supported under Dedicated/Private contracts.

Delivery & chain-of-custody
- Delivery options: presigned S3 + SHA256 manifest, secure SFTP with one-time credentials, or encrypted tar delivered to customer endpoint (TLS + PGP as needed).
- Each export includes a signed manifest (service cert) with byte-level checksums, event counts, time-range, and export-policy id. That manifest can be timestamped and notarized (we support AWS KMS signing or HSM-backed signatures for enterprise contracts).

Tamper evidence & auditability
- All export operations produce an immutable record in our audit ledger with export job id, initiator, and verification hashes.
- We can provide a signed proof-of-export (manifest + audit-log snapshot) suitable for legal preservation requests.

Performance knobs and recommendations
- We include recommended chunk sizes (default 1GB compressed per shard) and parallelism settings. For first-pass estimates, see Ben's deeper write-up (cc'd).

Attachments: echelon-export-playbook.pdf (playbook with examples), retention-matrix.csv (per-resource defaults).

—

Audrey — quick technical follow-up and sample manifest attached. Highlights: 

Manifest & non-overlap
- Sample manifest (attached file: export-manifest-schema.json) includes: export_id, tenant_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, shard_index, shard_count, file_name, byte_count, sha256_checksum, event_count, signed_by, signature, kms_key_id. Manifests are deterministic for a given export job id; hourly slices use closed-open intervals [start, end) to avoid overlap.

Resume & dedup semantics
- Incremental exports are driven by a monotonic sequence token per-tenant. Each exported event has a sequence_number. Resumption uses the last acknowledged sequence_number; receivers dedupe on sequence_number + tenant_id.
- For transfers interrupted mid-file, we recommend chunking at boundaries where each chunk is independently checksummed. Transfers use resumable HTTP(s) or multipart S3 uploads.

Redaction options
- Field-level redaction at export time is supported for a pre-approved set of fields (PII templates). For anything requiring custom logic we recommend redaction post-export in your pipeline; however, under Private/Dedicated contracts we can add export-time transforms.

Throughput and example timing
- Typical Dedicated pool (N1: 8xA10G equiv) observed export throughput: 200–450 MB/s aggregated (compressed) depending on compression ratio. For conservative planning assume 200 MB/s (≈720 GB/hr compressed).
- Example: 1 TB compressed (approx 1.3–1.6 TB raw) => ~1.4 hours at 720 GB/hr; plan for 2–3 hours including manifest generation, checksum, and delivery handshake.

Delivery & encryption
- Delivery options: presigned S3 (recommended) with object-level AES256 + transfer TLS; SFTP endpoint with one-time creds; or direct SCP to customer host. Objects include per-file SHA256; manifests include SHA256 for the entire job.

Next steps
- If Echelon wants export-time PII redaction, we can scope a change-order and provide an estimate.
- Happy to do a 30-min runbook walkthrough and a speed-test with a 10GB sample export.

—
